newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to split ASLK-CGER between bourse, Fortis.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to split ASLK-CGER between bourse, Fortis.

text.p: Belgian finance minister Philippe Maystadt said on Friday the government agreed to sell 14.9 percent in bank ASLK-CGER on the stock market this autumn.
A further 9.8 percent would be sold to Belgian-Dutch banking and insurance group Fortis.
"We are very advanced in our discussions with Fortis and should conclude a definitive accord in the near future," Maystadt said after the weekly cabinet meeting.
Fortis already owns 49.9 percent of ASLK following an initial part-privatisation in 1993.
Belgium at that time negotiated a put option to sell Fortis this 9.8 percent stake at a preset price.
Maystadt said the price had been renegotiated and the final sum would depend on the price ASLK shares would be floated at.
"The price Fortis pays cannot be less than the price set during the bourse listing," he said. He gave no details.
Maystadt said that to facilitate the listing it had been necessary to restructure ASLK -- currently two separate companies representing banking and insurance activities.
ASLK Insurance will become a subsidiary of the listed ASLK Bank.
The sale and listing will cut Belgium's stake in ASLK to 25.1 percent.
Maystadt said that although the state would only hold 0.1 percent of shares in the restructured ASLK Insurance -- a so-called golden share -- it would have a 25.1 percent blocking vote.
